name: The First of Its Kind: Firsts That Opened New Worlds
description: The first wheel, first coin, first flight, first footprint on the Moon: the moments when something happened for the first time and nothing was quite the same again.

checkpoints.name: Firsts in clay and bronze
checkpoints.note: The Wheel and Cuneiform appear in Mesopotamia, followed by the Epic of Gilgamesh, one of the oldest stories, and the Code of Hammurabi, a famous early law code. The Croeseid is among the first coins, and the Ancient Olympic Games begin.

checkpoints.name: Firsts before the modern age
checkpoints.note: Paper spreads from China, the University of Bologna becomes the oldest university in Europe still at work, and Gutenberg's printing press spreads knowledge. Magellan and Elcano's crew sail around the world, and a vaccine against smallpox is shown in 1796.

checkpoints.name: The steam and wire age
checkpoints.note: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway and the Penny Black make travel and post cheap. The daguerreotype and electric telegraph, and then the telephone and light bulb, change communication, while the Great Exhibition, a transcontinental railway and the Benz Patent-Motorwagen set the pace. The first modern Olympics follow in 1896.

checkpoints.name: Flight, film and the poles
checkpoints.note: The Wright Flyer takes off, A Trip to the Moon is an early science-fiction film, Amundsen reaches the South Pole, and penicillin is found. The Jazz Singer brings talking pictures, and the first World Cup and Academy Awards follow, with Snow White the first full-length cel-animated film, and ENIAC an early general-purpose electronic computer.

checkpoints.name: The space age and after
checkpoints.note: Everest is climbed, Sputnik 1 and Laika orbit the Earth, Yuri Gagarin and Valentina Tereshkova fly, and Neil Armstrong walks on the Moon in Apollo 11. Dolly the sheep is cloned, the World Wide Web spreads, and gravitational waves are detected in 2015.
